punchline: While astronomers hunted for longitude among the stars, a clockmaker solved it with a clock that kept time at sea.
thirty_sec: In the 1700s ships were lost because sailors could not find longitude. In 1714 Parliament offered a big prize and astronomers searched the sky. John Harrison, a self-taught clockmaker, built clocks that kept accurate time at sea instead. His H4 lost only about five seconds in 81 days on a voyage to Jamaica in 1761. Dava Sobel tells it in Longitude.
